newsitem.title: USA: NYCE cotton called to open little change.
newsitem.headline: NYCE cotton called to open little change.

text.p: NYCE cotton futures were called to open unchanged Thursday, based on market orders at 1020 EST, traders said.

But prices are expected to fall during the session on negative consumption data. U.S. ommerce Department put factory consumption in March at a seasonally-adjusted annual rate of 10,480 480-lb bales compared with 10,703 bales in February.
USDA reported commitments in the 1996/97 crop for the week ended April 17 at only 97,900 480-lb bales. Total commitments rose to 6,329,900 bales out of the 7.0 million bales forecast by USDA.
"The specs are still short but these numbers don't give them any reason to step up to the plate," Sharon Johnson, an analyst with Frank Schneider and Co Inc, said of the data.
Additionally, there were 198 delivery notices issued today, the first notice day for the May contract.
Support in most-active July was pegged at 73.00 cents, barely below the 10-day moving average of 73.04.
Wednesday, July finished up 0.55 cent at 73.45 cents a lb after trading from 73.50 to 72.76 cents. Spot May closed 0.29 cent higher at 71.37 cents.
